paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this task, you are to write an essay on the importance of developing a healthy lifestyle among college students. You will have 30 minutes for the task. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本任务中，您将写一篇关于大学生发展健康生活方式的重要性的文章。您将有 30 分钟的时间来完成该任务。您应该写至少 120 个字但不超过 180 个字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Parenting brings fathers more joy than it does mothers, according to a new study. The research examined three studies 26 more than 18,000 participants. Across all three, parenthood was 27 with more positive wellbeing outcomes for dads than for mums.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一项新的研究表明，养育孩子给父亲带来的快乐比母亲更多。该研究考察了三项涉及 18,000 多名参与者的研究。在这三者中，为人父母与父亲的幸福感比母亲更积极。

paragraphs.sourceText: So why are fathers happier than mothers? "Fathers may fare better than mothers in part due to how they spend time with their children," said lead author Katherine Nelson-Coffey. In one study, the authors 28 that dads were more likely to take "playing" as an 29 activity both when caring for their kids and spending time with their kids. "Playing with their children likely offers parents opportunities to experience positive feelings and 30 closeness with their children," they say.
paragraphs.translationZh: 那么为什么父亲比母亲更幸福呢？主要作者凯瑟琳·尼尔森-科菲说：“父亲的表现可能比母亲更好，部分原因在于他们与孩子共度时光的方式。”在一项研究中，作者指出，爸爸在照顾孩子和与孩子共度时光时更有可能将“玩耍”作为一项额外活动。他们说：“与孩子一起玩耍可能为父母提供了体验积极情绪并培养与孩子亲密关系的机会。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Fathers also did better than men without kids, reporting greater happiness, life satisfaction, and fewer 31 symptoms. They also reported greater connectedness and autonomy (自主). For mums, 32 , compared to women without children, the results weren't quite as positive. Mums reported greater autonomy, but also "greater trouble" and fewer positive 33 .
paragraphs.translationZh: 父亲们也比没有孩子的男性表现得更好，他们的幸福感、生活满意度更高，抑郁症状也更少。他们还报告了更大的连通性和自主性（自主）。然而，对于妈妈来说，与没有孩子的女性相比，结果并不那么积极。妈妈们报告说，她们有更大的自主权，但也有“更大的麻烦”和更少的积极情绪。

paragraphs.sourceText: Mums reported happier moods while interacting with their kids, compared to other experiences, but not while engaging 34 in childcare. "This difference suggests that how mothers and fathers spend time with their children might have important 35 for their wellbeing," the authors write. They suspect that mums may be less happy than dads because they're more likely to have higher expectations about parenthood. As such, they're more likely to be "let down" by the experience.
paragraphs.translationZh: 与其他经历相比，妈妈们在与孩子互动时的心情更快乐，但在直接参与育儿时却没有。作者写道：“这种差异表明，母亲和父亲与孩子共度时光的方式可能对他们的福祉产生重要影响。”他们怀疑妈妈可能没有爸爸那么快乐，因为她们更有可能对为人父母抱有更高的期望。因此，他们更有可能对这种经历感到“失望”。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Learning to say no
paragraphs.translationZh: 学会说不

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Not doing something will always be faster than doing it. This philosophy applies in many areas of life. For example, there is no meeting that goes faster than not having a meeting at all. This is not to say you should never attend another meeting, but the truth is that we say "yes" to too many things we don't actually want to do.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 不做某事总是比做某事更快。这种哲学适用于生活的许多领域。例如，没有比不开会更快的会议了。这并不是说您永远不应该参加其他会议，但事实是我们对太多我们实际上不想做的事情说“是”。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) How often do people ask you to do something and you just reply, "Sure." Three days later, you're overwhelmed by how much is on your to-do list. We become frustrated by our obligations even though we were the ones who said "yes" to them in the first place. Even worse, people will occasionally fight to do things that waste time. You don't have to do something just because it exists. It's worth asking if things are necessary. Many of them are not, and a simple "no" will be more productive than whatever work the most efficient person can cope with. But if the benefits of saying "no" are so obvious, then why do we say "yes" so often?
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 有多少次人们要求你做某事而你只是回答“当然”。三天后，你会对待办事项清单上的事情感到不知所措。即使我们是最初对这些义务说“是”的人，我们也会对自己的义务感到沮丧。更糟糕的是，人们偶尔会争着做一些浪费时间的事情。你不必仅仅因为某件事存在就去做它。值得一问的是是否有必要。他们中的许多人都不是，一个简单的“不”将比最有效率的人能够处理的任何工作更有效率。但如果说“不”的好处如此明显，那我们为什么还要经常说“是”呢？

paragraphs.sourceText: C) We say "yes" to many requests not because we want to do them, but because we don't want to be seen as rude or unhelpful. Often, we have to consider saying "no" to someone we will interact with again in the future — our co-worker, our spouse, our family and friends. Saying "no" to our superiors at work can be particularly difficult. In these situations, I like the approach recommended in Essentialism by Greg McKeown. He writes, "Remind your superiors what you would be neglecting if you said 'yes' and force them to deal with the trade-off. For example, if your manager comes to you and asks you to do X, you can respond with 'Yes, I'm happy to make this the priority. Which of these other projects should I deprioritize to pay attention to this new project?' "
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 我们对许多请求说“是”，并不是因为我们想做这些事情，而是因为我们不想被视为粗鲁或无助。通常，我们必须考虑对将来再次接触的人说“不”——我们的同事、配偶、家人和朋友。在工作中对上级说“不”可能特别困难。在这些情况下，我喜欢 Greg McKeown 在《本质主义》中推荐的方法。他写道：“提醒你的上级，如果你说‘是’，你会忽视什么，并迫使他们进行权衡。例如，如果你的经理来找你，要求你做某件事，你可以回答‘是的，我很高兴将此作为优先事项。我应该优先考虑哪些其他项目来关注这个新项目？’ ”

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Collaborating with others is an important element of life. The thought of straining the relationship outweighs the commitment of our time and energy. For this reason, it can be helpful to be gracious in your response. Do whatever favors you can, and be warm-hearted and direct when you have to say no. But even after we have accounted for these social considerations, many of us still seem to do a poor job of managing the trade-off between yes and no. We find ourselves over-committed to things that don't meaningfully improve or support those around us, and certainly don't improve our own lives.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 与他人合作是生活的重要组成部分。使关系紧张的想法比我们投入的时间和精力更重要。因此，礼貌地回应会很有帮助。尽你所能，当你不得不拒绝时，要热情而直接。但即使我们考虑了这些社会因素，我们中的许多人似乎仍然在管理是与否之间的权衡方面做得很差。我们发现自己过度致力于那些不会有效改善或支持我们周围人的事情，当然也不会改善我们自己的生活。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Perhaps one issue is how we think about the meaning of yes and no. The words "yes" and "no" get so often used in comparison with each other that it feels like they carry equal weight in conversation. In reality, they're not just opposite in meaning, but of entirely different magnitudes in commitment. When you say "no", you're only saying "no" to one option. When you say "yes", you're saying "no" to every other option. I like how economist Tim Harford put it, "Every time we say 'yes' to a request, we're also saying 'no' to anything else we might accomplish with the time." Once you're committed to something, you've already decided how that future block of time will be spent. In other words, saying "no" saves you time in the future. Saying "yes" costs you time in the future. "No" is a form of time credit. You retain the ability to spend your future time however you want. "Yes" is a form of time debt. You have to pay back your commitment at some point.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 也许一个问题是我们如何思考“是”和“否”的含义。 “是”和“否”这两个词经常被用来相互比较，以至于感觉它们在谈话中具有同等的重要性。事实上，它们不仅含义相反，而且承诺的程度也完全不同。当你说“不”时，你只是对一种选择说“不”。当你说“是”时，你就对所有其他选项说“不”。我喜欢经济学家蒂姆·哈福德的说法：“每次我们对一个请求说‘是’，我们也就对我们在这段时间里可能完成的任何其他事情说‘不’。”一旦你致力于某件事，你就已经决定了如何度过未来的时间。换句话说，说“不”可以节省你未来的时间。说“是”会浪费你未来的时间。 “不”是时间信用的一种形式。您仍然可以按照自己的意愿度过未来的时间。 “是”是一种时间债。你必须在某个时候偿还你的承诺。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) "No" is a decision. "Yes" is a responsibility. Saying "no" is sometimes seen as a luxury that only those in power can afford. And it's true: turning down opportunities is easier when you can fall back on the safety net provided by power, money, and authority. But it's also true that saying "no" is not merely a privilege reserved for the successful. It's also a strategy that can help you become successful. Saying "no" is an important skill to develop at any stage of your career because it retains the most important asset in life: your time. As investor Pedro Sorrentino put it, "If you don't guard your time, people will steal it from you." You need to say "no" to whatever isn't leading you toward your goals.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) “不”是一个决定。 “是”是一种责任。说“不”有时被视为只有当权者才能承受的奢侈。确实如此：当你可以依靠权力、金钱和权威提供的安全网时，拒绝机会就会更容易。但事实上，说“不”不仅仅是成功者的特权。这也是一种可以帮助您取得成功的策略。说“不”是在职业生涯的任何阶段都需要培养的一项重要技能，因为它保留了生命中最重要的资产：你的时间。正如投资者佩德罗·索伦蒂诺(Pedro Sorrentino)所说，“如果你不保护自己的时间，人们就会从你身边偷走它。”你需要对任何不能引导你实现目标的事情说“不”。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Nobody embodied this idea better than Steve Jobs, who said, "People think focus means saying 'yes' to the thing you've got to focus on. But that's not what it means at all. It means saying 'no' to the hundred other good ideas that there are. You have to pick carefully." Jobs had another great quote about saying "no": "I'm actually as proud of the things we haven't done as the things I have done. Innovation is saying 'no' to 1,000 things."
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 没有人比史蒂夫·乔布斯更能体现这一理念，他说：“人们认为专注意味着对你必须关注的事情说‘是’。但这根本不是这个意思。它意味着对其他上百个好主意说‘不’。你必须仔细选择。”乔布斯还有一句关于说“不”的精彩名言：“事实上，我对我们没有做过的事情和我所做的事情一样感到自豪。创新就是对 1000 件事说‘不’。”

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Over time, as you continue to improve and succeed, your strategy needs to change. The opportunity cost of your time increases as you become more successful. At first, you just eliminate the obvious distractions and explore the rest. As your skills improve and you learn to separate what works from what doesn't, you have to continually increase your threshold for saying "yes". You still need to say "no" to distractions, but you also need to learn to say "no" to opportunities that were previously good uses of time, so you can make space for better uses of time. It's a good problem to have, but it can be a tough skill to master.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 随着时间的推移，当你不断进步并取得成功时，你的策略需要改变。随着您变得更加成功，您的时间机会成本也会增加。首先，您只需消除明显的干扰并探索其余的。随着你的技能不断提高，你学会区分什么有效，什么无效，你必须不断提高说“是”的门槛。你仍然需要对干扰说“不”，但你也需要学会对以前很好地利用时间的机会说“不”，这样你就可以腾出空间来更好地利用时间。这是一个好问题，但它可能是一项很难掌握的技能。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) What is true about health is also true about productivity: an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure. More effort is wasted doing things that don't matter than is wasted doing things inefficiently. And if that is the case, elimination is a more useful skill than optimization. I'm reminded of the famous Peter Drucker quote, "There is nothing so useless as doing efficiently that which should not be done at all."
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 关于健康的真理对于生产力也是如此：一分预防胜于一分治疗。浪费在无关紧要的事情上的精力比浪费在效率低下的事情上的精力还要多。如果是这样的话，消除是比优化更有用的技能。我想起了彼得·德鲁克的名言：“没有什么比有效地做根本不应该做的事情更无用的了。”

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. People often grant a request just because they want to appear polite and helpful.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 人们常常只是因为想显得有礼貌和乐于助人而同意请求。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. It's no easy job learning to say "no" to opportunities that were once considered worth grasping.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 学会对曾经被认为值得抓住的机会说“不”并不是一件容易的事。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. When you decline a request, you are saving your future time.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 当你拒绝请求时，你就节省了未来的时间。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. People sometimes struggle to do things that are simply a waste of time.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 人们有时会努力做一些纯粹浪费时间的事情。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Doing efficiently what is not worth doing is the most useless effort.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40、高效地做不值得做的事，是最无用的努力。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. It is especially difficult for people to decline to do what their superiors ask them to do.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 人们很难拒绝做上级要求他们做的事。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. People agree to do too many things they are in fact unwilling to do.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42.人们同意做太多他们实际上不愿意做的事情。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. According to one famous entrepreneur, innovation means refusal to do an enormous number of things.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 一位著名企业家认为，创新意味着拒绝做大量的事情。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. It is an essential aspect of life to cooperate with other people.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 与他人合作是生活的一个重要方面。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Refusing a request is sometimes seen as a privilege not enjoyed by ordinary people.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 拒绝请求有时被视为普通人不享有的特权。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: We're eating more fish than ever these days. At around 20 kilograms per person global fish consumption is now more than twice what it was in the 1960s. What's really remarkable, though, is where that fish comes from.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这些天我们吃的鱼比以往任何时候都多。目前全球鱼类消费量约为人均 20 公斤，是 20 世纪 60 年代的两倍多。不过，真正值得注意的是这些鱼的产地。

paragraphs.sourceText: For the first time in human history, most of our aquatic (水产的) food now comes from farming rather than fishing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 人类历史上第一次，我们的大部分水产食品现在来自农业而不是渔业。

paragraphs.sourceText: People ate around 73 million tonnes of farmed fish — just more than half of the volume of fish that humans consumed — in 2014. That's out of a total fish supply of 167 million tonnes; the remaining 20 million or so tonnes go into things like animal feed and medical products.
paragraphs.translationZh: 2014 年，人们食用了约 7300 万吨养殖鱼，仅占人类消费鱼量的一半以上。这还不包括 1.67 亿吨的鱼类供应总量；剩下的 2000 万吨左右用于生产动物饲料和医疗产品等。

paragraphs.sourceText: To keep eating fish at the current rate, we're definitely going to need to keep aquaculture (水产养殖) developing. That's because the volume of fish caught in the wild has leveled off since the 1990s.
paragraphs.translationZh: 为了保持目前的吃鱼速度，我们肯定需要保持水产养殖的发展。这是因为自 20 世纪 90 年代以来，野外捕获的鱼类数量已趋于平稳。

paragraphs.sourceText: Back in 1974, only 10% of marine fish stocks had been overfished. Now, more than three-tenths are. Only a tenth of our oceans' fish stocks could sustain heavier fishing than current levels.
paragraphs.translationZh: 早在 1974 年，只有 10% 的海洋鱼类遭到过度捕捞。现在，超过十分之三。我们海洋中只有十分之一的鱼类资源能够维持比目前水平更高的捕捞量。

paragraphs.sourceText: But while catchings at sea have suffered, fish-farming has been growing at a fast rate. A lot of that is coming from China, which produces 60% of the world's farmed fish. In fact, some 35 countries, including China, now produce more farmed than wild-caught fish.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管海上捕捞量受到影响，但养鱼业却在快速增长。其中很大一部分来自中国，中国生产的养殖鱼类占全球的 60%。事实上，包括中国在内的大约 35 个国家目前养殖鱼类的产量超过了野生捕捞的鱼类。

paragraphs.sourceText: This shift toward aquaculture isn't just good for ensuring salmon (三文鱼) on your plate; it's also crucial to ensuring food security and sustainability. By 2050, the world will need to feed an estimated 9.7 billion people. They'll have to get their protein somewhere. However, raising cattle, pigs, and other land-based animals requires vast sums of grain and water. For example, pound for pound, beef requires 15 times more feed to raise than carp, a freshwater fish farmed all over Asia. That grain — and the water needed to grow it — could be consumed by people instead.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这种向水产养殖的转变不仅有利于确保三文鱼出现在您的餐桌上，而且还有助于确保您的餐桌上有三文鱼。这对于确保粮食安全和可持续性也至关重要。到 2050 年，世界将需要养活大约 97 亿人。他们必须从某个地方获取蛋白质。然而，饲养牛、猪和其他陆生动物需要大量的粮食和水。例如，按重量计算，饲养牛肉所需的饲料是鲤鱼（一种亚洲各地养殖的淡水鱼）的 15 倍。这些谷物——以及种植谷物所需的水——可以被人们消费。

paragraphs.sourceText: However, aquaculture is no silver bullet. In some southeast Asian countries, shrimp farming does disastrous damage to marine ecosystems. Despite these problems, however, shrimp continues to be among the most popular seafoods worldwide.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，水产养殖并不是灵丹妙药。在一些东南亚国家，虾类养殖对海洋生态系统造成了灾难性的破坏。然而，尽管存在这些问题，虾仍然是世界上最受欢迎的海鲜之一。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: In 2020, the Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to the World Food Programme (WFP).
paragraphs.translationZh: 2020年，诺贝尔和平奖授予世界粮食计划署（WFP）。

paragraphs.sourceText: Why a Nobel Prize for the WFP, and why now? In 2019, the WFP assisted nearly 100 million people in 88 countries. It is the safety net for those who fall off the edge of existence. It is a response to solving the problem of food instability. Its Nobel Prize reminds us all of the moral hazard in imagining that the poor and vulnerable are somebody else's problem.
paragraphs.translationZh: 为什么世界粮食计划署获得诺贝尔奖，为什么是现在？ 2019年，粮食计划署向88个国家的近1亿人提供了援助。它是那些脱离生存边缘的人的安全网。这是解决粮食不稳定问题的回应。它的诺贝尔奖提醒我们所有人，将穷人和弱势群体视为别人的问题是存在道德风险的。

paragraphs.sourceText: The WFP has been around since 1961 and has been the global coordinator of nationally based efforts to avoid disasters with food aid. Despite decades of effort to eliminate hunger, the latest estimate is that about 11% of people on the planet (about 820 million people) are suffering daily undernourishment. Progress at reducing undernourishment has stopped despite gains through the 1990s and 2000s.
paragraphs.translationZh: 粮食计划署自 1961 年成立以来，一直是各国通过粮食援助避免灾害的努力的全球协调者。尽管人们为消除饥饿付出了数十年的努力，但最新估计，地球上约有 11% 的人（约 8.2 亿人）每天都遭受营养不良。尽管 20 世纪 90 年代和 2000 年代取得了进展，但减少营养不良的进展已经停止。

paragraphs.sourceText: Developed countries sometimes offer food and aid to developing ones, but at a price. One American philosopher stated that addressing the needs of the poor and vulnerable is about more than money — it is mostly about creating conditions under which prosperity and opportunity can thrive. When aid is offered with heavy conditions attached, like loan repayment or food for resources, it often widens the gap between rich and poor and sustains the old world order. This is why the work of the WFP is so vital.
paragraphs.translationZh: 发达国家有时会向发展中国家提供粮食和援助，但要付出一定的代价。一位美国哲学家表示，解决穷人和弱势群体的需求不仅仅是金钱的问题，更重要的是创造繁荣和机会蓬勃发展的条件。当提供附加严格条件的援助时，例如偿还贷款或以粮食换取资源，它往往会扩大贫富差距并维持旧的世界秩序。这就是粮食计划署的工作如此重要的原因。

paragraphs.sourceText: The scientific community, however, can provide a helping hand to the WFP. By sharing knowledge of agriculture and climate with peers in countries most vulnerable to poverty and hunger, scientists can help reduce these problems. By making its voice heard, science can lead by example. The ability to overcome food shortages that must be built into some of the poorest countries will not come from loans from wealthy countries, which may have food problems of their own, or world economic institutions. This ability will be built upon self-confident people using open and shared scientific knowledge to pull themselves out of their misery.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，科学界可以向粮食计划署提供帮助。通过与最容易遭受贫困和饥饿的国家的同行分享农业和气候知识，科学家可以帮助减少这些问题。通过发出自己的声音，科学可以以身作则。一些最贫穷国家必须建立克服粮食短缺的能力，但这种能力不会来自富裕国家或世界经济机构的贷款，因为富裕国家可能有自己的粮食问题。这种能力将建立在自信的人们使用开放和共享的科学知识来摆脱痛苦的基础上。
